newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks shake off losses to end higher.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks shake off losses to end higher.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks shrugged off the day's losses to end up on Friday, lifted by bargain-hunting in the property sector after selling during most of the week pulled share prices down to oversold levels, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index rose 16.97 points, or 0.14 percent, to 12,489.30 after falling to an early low of 12,331.63. Turnover was HK$10.58 billion compared with HK$9.28 billion on Thursday.
"It just snapped a bit of a losing streak," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
The index had three losing sessions in a row before Friday's gain and lost 247.23 points, or 1.94 percent, this week.
"I think that Hong Kong has overreacted to the interest rate scenario," said Osborn.
Analysts said the Hong Kong market had already factored a 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates into share prices.
The U.S. Federal Reserve meets next Tuesday to deliberate interest rates. Brokers said a 25 basis point hike would clear market uncertainty and stocks could rebound next week.
"If interest rates are going to be raised by 0.25 percent, the impact will be neutral," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.

"But if they are raised by more, that will be negative." In the property sector, shares in Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd rose HK$1.25 to HK$68.50 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd advanced HK$0.50 to HK$64.00.
"There was some bargain-hunting going on in the property developers with good response to (property) pre-sales and continued increases in property prices," said So.
Shares in Wharf Holdings Ltd gained HK$0.10 to HK$29.15. The Hong Kong conglomerate posted a 24 percent fall in 1996 net profit to HK$2.74 billion.
Hopewell Holdings Ltd was due to report interim results after the close. It fell HK$0.025 to HK$4.10.
Beijing Datang Power Generation Co Ltd made its market debut on Friday. The stock opened at HK$3.00 compared with an issue price of HK$2.52 and closed at HK$3.025.
Datang Power operates coal-fired electric power plants which supply electricity to Beijing and other industrial cities in northern China.
Property redevelopment firm Soundwill Holdings Ltd also made its trading debut on Friday, opening at HK$2.90 per share compared with an issue price of HK$2.18 and closing at HK$2.675.
